statement.p: Curves C_1 and C_2 are parametrized as follows: C_1 \mbox{ is } (x(t),y(t)) = (t,0)\quad\mbox{ for } -1\le t\le1 and C_2 \mbox{ is } (x(t),y(t)) = (\cos t,\sin t) \quad\mbox{ for } 0 \le t\le \pi.
Sketch, on a separate sheet of paper, the curves C_1 and C_2 with arrows showing their orientation.
Next, suppose that \vec F = 2 x\,\vec i + (5 x + 7 y)\,\vec j. Calculate \int_C\vec F\cdot d\vec r, where C is the curve given by C=C_1+C_2.

static.solution: On C_1, only the \vec i-component of \vec F contributes to the integral. There d\vec r=\vec i\,dy, so \int_{C_1}\vec F\cdot d\vec r = \int_{-1}^1 2 x\vec i\cdot \vec i\,dy = \int_{-1}^1 2 x\,dx = \frac{x^2}{2}\Bigg|_{-1}^1 = 0. On C_2, we have \vec r'(t) = -\sin t\,\vec i + \cos t\,\vec j, so \int_{C_2}\vec F\cdot d\vec r = \int_{0}^{\pi}(2\,\cos(t)\,\vec i + (5\,\cos(t) + 7\,\sin(t))\,\vec j)\cdot (-\sin t\,\vec i +\cos t\,\vec j)\, dt = \int_{0}^{\pi} 5\,\cos(t)\sin(t) + 5\,\cos^2(t)\,dt = \frac{5}{2}\,\pi.
